title: Radhika Madan Says Irrfan Khan Taught Her Never Stop Being Student
excerpt: Recalling Angrezi Medium, Madan describes finding Irrfan rehearsing before a key scene and learning that even a master never stopped learning.
body:
• Radhika Madan says working with Irrfan Khan on Angrezi Medium shaped her as an actor, in remarks resurfacing in Indian Express coverage.
  • Her central memory: finding Irrfan, despite his stature, rehearsing nervously before an important scene — "he was still a student."
  • She has repeated the lesson for years: "Never stop being a student of life, no matter where you reach."
  • Angrezi Medium (2020), directed by Homi Adajania, was one of Irrfan's final films; he died in April 2020.

Radhika Madan has recalled, again, the lesson she took from working with Irrfan Khan on Angrezi Medium: never stop being a student. The remarks, carried in Koimoi's report of her IANS interview and echoed in her later interviews, centre on a single night-before-a-scene memory that she says gave her a learning for a lifetime.

Madan played Tarika, the daughter of Irrfan's Champak Bansal, a father who goes to great lengths to support his daughter's dream of studying abroad. The 2020 film, directed by Homi Adajania, also stars Dimple Kapadia, Pankaj Tripathi, Deepak Dobriyal and Ranvir Shorey, according to Filmfare.

The Rehearsal She Never Forgot

"We were going to shoot a very important scene in the film. I was very nervous about it and I was just roaming with the script here and there. I saw a tall man doing the same thing and wondered who is the person doing the same thing. Then, when I went closer I realized it was Irrfan sir."

— Radhika Madan, speaking to IANS

She drew the conclusion immediately. "I got to learn that it must have been his nth film and he was still a student. He still got tense before an important scene, he was still rehearsing. It was such a big lesson and my favorite memory from the sets. He was still a student and I would want to imbibe that in me. I learned that I should never stop being a student, no matter what," she said.

She returned to the same memory on Teacher's Day in 2023, telling media, in remarks reported by Indulge Express: "The learning that never stop being a student, was imbibed by Irrfan sir. And I remember that like before an important scene a night before he was always seen with a script rehearsing, and he didn't need to at that stature, and at that position."

"He Said the Most When He Didn't Say Anything"

Madan has also described learning from Irrfan's presence rather than his instruction. "First of all the film had such an ensemble cast where I could just sit and learn so much. I didn't have to do anything. Everyone was a 'diggaj' (dignitary) if I may say so. I think Irrfan sir said the most when he didn't say anything. His eyes, demeanour, everything was so expressive. So words were not important when it comes to him," she said.

She added that the set protected his health. Irrfan had been treated for a neuroendocrine tumour, and the team was told his shots would be taken first and his health was the priority. "I didn't get the opportunity to talk to him one-on-one a lot because he had to conserve his energy a lot. He didn't have to say anything and he could still teach the other person so many things by the way he was," she said.

A Lesson Repeated Across Years

"Working with him in Angrezi Medium really shaped me as an actor. Because he is one guy who always tells the truth. And he never makes a false note. He never stopped learning."

— Radhikka Madan, to Filmfare

On Irrfan's death anniversary in April 2025, she told Filmfare she still watches his films, and has watched Angrezi Medium multiple times "because sometimes I have to pinch myself to realise that I actually got to work with him." She captioned behind-the-scenes photos: "The 'Tarika' in me is still alive! This little girl with big dreams in her eyes, the drive to conquer the world and take on anything that life offers her!"

Irrfan died in April 2020, weeks after the film's release, of complications arising from a neuroendocrine tumour. His performance in Angrezi Medium, one of his final films, posthumously earned him Best Actor in a Leading Role at the Filmfare Awards, and he was honoured with a Lifetime Achievement award at the 66th Filmfare Awards. For diaspora viewers who discovered Irrfan through both Hindi cinema and international films, Madan's account is a reminder of why his co-stars keep returning to the same word: student.
